text:
Both responses get the arithmetic right. The ethanol volume is 375 mL × 0.048 = 18 mL. Its mass is 18 × 0.789 = 14.2 g. That gives ≈1.42 standard drinks. Both also show the same three key steps, so they are equal on correctness and reasoning.

The difference is clarity and economy. Response A wraps the same steps in a lot of filler: "Thank you for your question," "To begin," "Next," "Finally," and "In summary, based on the calculation above." This padding pushes it to roughly 114 words, close to the 120-word limit, without adding anything useful. It also has a small notation slip ("= ≈1.42") and writes "= 14.2 g" when the value is rounded.

Response B states the answer up front and shows the same steps cleanly. It adds one useful, accurate detail: Australian labels give standard drinks to one decimal place, so the can would be labelled 1.4. That is the kind of extra content that earns its words.

Since correctness and reasoning are equal, B wins on clarity and concision.

Verdict: B
